claims.statement: build-win/ is a pre-configured CMake build tree (CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Windows, x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++-posix from /home/jambo/buildkit/mingw/root, Ninja, Release); a plain `cmake --build build-win --target TONE3000_Standalone` produces build-win/plugin/TONE3000_artefacts/Release/Standalone/TONE3000.exe, a self-contained PE32+ x86-64 exe whose DLL imports must be Windows API DLLs only (no libstdc++/libgcc/libwinpthread). (test/CMakeLists.txt cited only as the repo's CMakeLists reference; the windows-build rule lives in docs.)

The root CMakeLists.txt carries two idempotent MinGW configure-time patches that ASIO and DirectWrite need under MinGW and must be kept: T3K_MINGW_ASIO_SEH (rewrite the ASIO SDK's C-style __try/__except SEH to if/else in juce_audio_devices/asio/WINASIO.cpp) and T3K_MINGW_DWRITE_CRP (route IDWriteFactory::CreateCustomRenderingParams through the base COM interface in juce_graphics/fonts/juce_DirectWriteTypeface.cpp, whose MinGW header hides it behind the vtable). ASIO is a hard user requirement, ON by default via JUCE's bundled ASIO SDK. MinGW's libstdc++ lacks std::tanhf/std::floorf, so the codebase uses std::tanh/std::floor with float args.

Wine smoke test on WSLg: WINEPREFIX=/home/jambo/wine-test WINEDEBUG=-all DISPLAY=:0 wineboot -u, then timeout --signal=KILL 30 wine64 TONE3000.exe; exit 124 (had to SIGKILL a live app) means success, and an ALSA /dev/snd/seq 'No such file' line is expected with no audio device. Wine has no real ASIO driver, so this proves launch but not the ASIO dropdown; static proof the ASIO type compiled in is strings TONE3000.exe | grep -i ASIOAudioIODevice.

script/win-standalone.sh (folded into script/ by the repo-organization reorg) is env-driven: it loads the gitignored .env (documented in .env.example) and stages the built TONE3000.exe to ${T3K_STAGE_DIR}/TONE3000-win-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS (run-timestamp only, never descriptive suffixes), with -2/-3 dir dedup, md5sums, and the git branch + HEAD commit printed for provenance. T3K_STAGE_DIR gotcha: unset, the default `ls -d /mnt/c/Users/*/Downloads | head -1` glob picks the FIRST alphabetical user dir, which on this box is a broken/empty stub `/mnt/c/Users/Default User/Downloads` — NOT jambo — so staging silently lands in the wrong user folder; .env.example sets T3K_STAGE_DIR=/mnt/c/Users/jambo/Downloads to fix it. A plain build does not pick up a changed .env (publishable key) or new sources — it needs a reconfigure (GLOB re-runs) ~2 min per docs/agents/windows-build.md.

Optional Authenticode signing (commit 3969401): with T3K_SIGN=1 in .env, win-standalone.sh signs the STAGED copy after cp (never the build-tree exe) via ${T3K_SIGNING_DIR:-$HOME/signing}/sign-exe.sh, keyed by T3K_SIGN_CERT (p12 basename), T3K_SIGN_PASS, T3K_SIGN_TS (RFC3161 URL, default http://timestamp.sectigo.com) and T3K_SIGN_VERIFY (post-sign chain check, default 1); a signing failure leaves the staged exe unsigned and fails the script. Certs/keys live outside the repo (default $HOME/signing; *.p12/*.cer gitignored, never committed); the repo ships env-driven, machine-path-free helpers script/signing/{sign-exe,build-minica,make-demo-cert,add-cert}.sh. osslsigncode 2.13 gotchas (verified live): password flag is -pass (-p means proxy), -in/-out, -out refuses existing files (sign to temp + mv), self-signed roots need verify -CAfile. build-minica.sh builds a local trust chain (25 y root + 10 y codeSigning leaf, no-password p12 + .pem/root.pem) and add-cert.sh folds a commercial CA intermediate into <cert>-full.p12 for real publisher trust.
